Latest Update: Why England fans booed Arsenal defender Ben White again after Croatia win

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (504 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readarsenal

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ben White returned to the England senior squad on Thursday night but received a hostile reception at Wembley.
  • The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.
  • Sources indicate that thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben White returned to the England senior squad on Thursday night but received a hostile reception at Wembley.

The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.

Sources indicate that thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad. However, this raises questions as to why some England supporters have turned on the defender after he has continued to perform well for Arsenal.

The answer lies with the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

White left the England World Cup camp in November 2022, returning home due to personal reasons. The FA confirmed that White will not return to the squad and asked that his privacy be respected.

He did not play in the first two group games for England and missed the last group game against Wales due to illness.

There were reports that White had fallen out with assistant manager Steve Holland, but neither the FA nor England management confirmed this was the reason he left.

Gareth Southgate later stated there were no problems between White and Holland and that White had simply withdrawn himself from selection after the tournament.

This meant that White would never play for England again while Southgate was still manager. Some fans were clearly upset by this, as they felt White was shunning his country.

When White returned under Tuchel in March 2026, he was met with a negative reaction. He was booed by the crowd when he scored his first-ever international goal against Uruguay. White was also booed in the same fashion against Japan.

He has since explained that supporters might view the situation differently if they knew the full story. However, he has chosen not to reveal the private details behind his departure.

Tuchel has shown little concern about White being affected by the controversy.

The England boss stated after the win on Thursday that he had not heard any boos and praised White’s qualities, work ethic and desire to play for his country.

He believes White can help England win games and added that he has the backing of the coaching staff.

Arsenal fans will be unsurprised to learn that White is still a valuable asset for Mikel Arteta, offering defensive consistency and being able to play as a right or centre-back.

The bad press that White is receiving from England fans will not go away any time soon. However, he has not done anything to hurt his reputation at club level. The reasons why he left for the World Cup are personal.

The main focus for Arsenal will be getting him match fit again. As for the England fans, we shall see.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, Diego Moreira scored his first goal for Belgium and AC Milan will be very happy to see their investment continuing to shine.

It has been revealed that it’s fair to say that Moreira has been a revelation for Milan. His arrival came out of nowhere, with a deal first reported by FootballKush and then it was picked up by the biggest sources in football. His first appearance was a struggle against Juventus, but the rest, as they say, is history.

Goals have come regularly, with huge appearances that have defined the Rossoneri’s season already. For example, the goal against Inter, with two assists to accompany it. He’s perhaps been the signing of the season in Italy and there’d maybe be a conversation about Europe, too.

After scoring against Italy, Moreira spoke to Sky, looking at the team’s performance, playing with Kevin De Bruyne and the feeling of grabbing his first goal for his country, as MilanNews relays.

“I’m very happy with my first goal for the national team. It was a special moment because my family was there. It’s a day I’ll always remember.”.

Mancini said that you deserved to win and that you are a very strong team….

“We have some very strong players up front, like Doku, De Bruyne, but I think that in the end it’s a sport where everyone is needed and we all played a great game.”.

What does it mean to play with a player like De Bruyne?

“De Bruyne is special; it’s a pleasure to have him with us because he sees things that others don’t see, he has a lot of experience and we’re happy to have him in our team.”.

What do you take from this experience with the national team at AC Milan?

“I learned a lot in Italy because it’s a league with a lot of experienced players. Playing for the national team and for AC Milan are two very positive things, and I’m very happy.”.

How do you recover in Europe after a difficult start?

“It’s difficult but we’re working towards this. We have to be prepared and we have players who will help us with this.”.

Then, in the mixed zone, he was also intercepted by MilanNews, where he also answered a few questions about the Rossoneri.

Diego, you scored in your first Milan derby, just like Kaká, Shevchenko, and Ronaldinho before you. How have you settled in at AC Milan?

“I’m very happy. At AC Milan, I’m surrounded by a special group, with many great players. Having them around me helps me a lot, especially in terms of experience. It’s true, the match against Inter was special. I’ll continue to work hard and give my best.”.

Good in Serie A, bad in the Europa League: why this two-faced Milan?

“I’m on the national team right now, and you’re asking me about Milan?”.

Belgium practically overwhelmed Italy, your current footballing nation. It ended 4-1, but the scoreline could have been eight or nine goals….

“It’s something special, and we’re very happy. It was an crucial match, so winning and scoring was really nice.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal look to build on their recent win over Liverpool as they return to the Emirates Stadium but will face an impressive London City Lionesses side who are a potent attacking threat on their travels.

Renée Slegers’ team have struggled to convert their strong performances into points in the league this season. They have lost their last four WSL games at home, however, becoming the first team in WSL history to draw four successive games at home.

In a recent development, their bad run must come to an end. They have taken just three points from their first nine league games so far this season, scoring a miserable total of 10 goals. However, they look like they have more in the tank and will need to be much more clinical in front of the goal.

Industry observers note that the day also marks Slegers’ 50th game in charge of the WSL. The Dutch manager has only lost six league games so far this season, with only Chelsea having a better record from teams that have been ever-present in the division.

Arsenal can’t take their opposition lightly after London City’s impressive recent form. They have won two and drawn once in their last three away league games, scoring 12 goals.

In a recent development, eder Maestre’s side has become a potent attacking force. Daniëlle van de Donk has provided four assists this season, and Delphine Cascarino has scored three goals and provided two assists.

Kadidiatou Diani can be dangerous. She has scored or assisted in all four of her league games away from home this season.

It has been revealed that london City’s attacking prowess means they are a far different proposition to some teams Arsenal have faced at home. They have been in a positive situation for 62.7 per cent of their league minutes this season, the highest in the WSL.

Arsenal will have to deal with the attacking threats but look to utilise their ball possession better. Giving London City an opportunity to counter could make an already tough afternoon even tougher.

Alessia Russo comes into the game having found the net in her last three WSL games and will be key in converting Arsenal’s chances into goals.

Recent findings suggest that the Gunners also revealed their fighting spirit in their midweek clash against Barcelona. They drew 1-1 at Camp Nou to become the first side to take points off the Spanish giants in the Women’s Champions League at home since April 2024.

Slegers’ team will feel emboldened by that result but will have to change their tactics against London City.

It has been revealed that they have won all seven games against Arsenal so far, scoring an impressive 22 goals and only conceding once. However, given London City’s recent away form, they will be hotly favoured.

They certainly have the quality to take all three points, but they must finally convert their dominance into a comfortable home win.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 14:04.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has reportedly prepared to enter talks over the Old Trafford future of Bruno Fernandes.

The 54-year-old Argentine arrives at the Theatre of Dreams with the Red Devils sitting 18th in the Premier League table after winning just one of their opening 10 top-flight games of 2026-27.

That woeful run was eventually enough to remove Michael Carrick from his post at Man Utd, with the club's hierarchy moving rapidly to lure Pochettino away from his duties with the United States on the international scene.

As well as Carrick, wonderkid JJ Gabriel has also departed the Red Devils this month, with the teenage sensation set to sign for European giants Real Madrid despite failing to make a first-team appearance for United.

Looking to avoid an unthinkable relegation this season, Man Utd are plotting significant additions to the playing squad during the January transfer window, with a Greek striker supposedly catching the eye.

According to transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano via Football Transfers, fresh Manchester United head coach Pochettino is set to be immediately involved in major talks at the Theatre of Dreams.

The report states that the Red Devils and captain Fernandes have been locked in discussions over a contract extension for the past five months, with an agreement yet to be reached by the two parties.

The 32-year-old's current deal at Old Trafford expires in June 2027, meaning that the Portuguese playmaker would be able to depart on a free transfer at the conclusion of this season.

It is understood that Man Utd are aiming to avoid that scenario, and now incoming boss Pochettino is set to join talks with the player and the club over the future of the influential attacker.

Fernandes supposedly retains interest from clubs in Italy, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, with Champions League-competing Galatasaray attempting to bring the former Sporting Lisbon man to Istanbul over the summer.

Whilst Manchester United's transfer activity since the exit of Sir Alex Ferguson has come under deserved criticism, there is no doubt that the signing of Fernandes was an excellent move by the fallen English powerhouses.

The 32-year-old has been an almost ever-present in the Red Devils ranks since joining from the Primeira Liga in January 2020, scoring 113 goals across a total of 341 competitive appearances.

Fernandes broke the Premier League assist record last season despite his side's immense struggles, and that theme of shining amid the chaos extends throughout the attacker's time in England.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Dowman has added another incredible achievement to his burgeoning career after becoming the youngest player to play for the England Under-21s.

Recent findings suggest that the Arsenal youngster was introduced from the bench in Friday’s 1-0 friendly loss to Portugal at Ashton Gate. The 16-year-10-month-13-day-old player is over three months younger than Jude Bellingham was when he played his first game for the Under-21s.

Sources indicate that dowman replaced former Arsenal academy player Amario Cozier-Duberry in the 61st minute. He came on alongside debutant Trey Nyoni as England tried to shift the momentum of a challenging game.

An early strike from Afonso Moreira gave Portugal the lead in the 28th minute. An ineffective England team failed to respond. However, the replacements gave Lee Carsley’s team some late momentum.

Despite the hosts’ attempts to level the score, they failed to break down the Portuguese defence. The result means England have lost for the second game running. However, Dowman had much to be pleased with personally.

Dowman has added to his growing collection of records.

He became the youngest player to play in the Champions League, the youngest goalscorer in the history of the Premier League and the youngest to win the Premier League title.

Breaking Bellingham’s England Under-21 record is another significant step. It shows how quickly Dowman has progressed through the international age groups.

He has already made a massive impression at Arsenal with Mikel Arteta’s love of giving younger players a chance, but Dowman will have some stiff competition for first team minutes.

Recent findings suggest that another positive is his progression on an international scale. He will improve both physically and tactically playing against older players and gain experience at a higher level.

According to recent reports, england will host France in their next friendly on Monday, 16th November. Dowman will be hoping to feature after his instant impact on the record books.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:04.

Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.

Palace have spent 14 consecutive seasons in the Premier League, and the capital club's board have taken drastic action to ensure that number becomes 15 at the end of the current campaign.

The Selhurst Park outfit entered the November international break in dire straits after a 3-1 loss to Andoni Iraola's Liverpool, marking their fourth consecutive top-flight defeat following setbacks against rivals Brighton & Hove Albion, Newcastle United and Tottenham Hotspur.

Particularly striking during that run were their struggles in front of goal and defensive frailties, highlighted by an alarming 12-1 aggregate score across those defeats that ultimately cost Sage his job.

Frank's reputation suffered during his spell as Spurs boss last season, but his previous work at Brentford should give the Selhurst Park faithful confidence that a turnaround is possible.

Nonetheless, it remains to be seen whether the Dane has conveyed his ideas in less than a week of training, with the international break also denying him access to his full squad, as the London club seek to end their four-match losing sequence.

A first victory since October and third overall would lift them above this weekend's 17th-placed hosts and potentially out of the bottom three, although the latter outcome depends on results elsewhere.

Coventry's 3-1 defeat at Everton before the pause left Frank Lampard's men alongside Arsenal and Manchester City as the only clubs yet to draw in this season's Premier League campaign.

However, while the defending champions and Man City occupy positions in the top three, Coventry's nine points leave them just one clear of the relegation places heading into a busy period.

Lampard's men can take encouragement from collecting six of those points in front of their adoring supporters, who witnessed October victories of 4-1 over Newcastle and 3-1 against Sunderland either side of a narrow 1-0 defeat to Fulham.

Although the absence of home clean sheets remains concerning, the Sky Blues' seven goals across their last three matches at the Coventry Building Society Arena represent clear progress after they failed to score in opening defeats to Hull City (1-0) and Brighton (5-0).

Now, the West Midlands side aim to secure consecutive home Premier League victories to avoid slipping into the bottom three.

Crystal Palace Premier League form:.

Crystal Palace form (all competitions):.

Caleb Yirenkyi and Bobby Thomas (calf) are doubtful for Coventry this weekend, while Luke Woolfenden (knee) and Josh Eccles (ankle) face late fitness tests; however, Frank Onyeka, Aurele Amenda (calf), Haji Wright (thigh) and Ephron Mason-Clark (knee) are expected to miss out.

Jack Rudoni is the only home player to have scored more than once, with the attacking midfielder's three goals accounting for 30% of the Sky Blues' tally of 10 this term.

After registering assists in consecutive appearances against Newcastle and Spurs in October, Brandon Thomas-Asante has dropped to the bench, but the Ghanaian forward will hope to play a pivotal role for Lampard's team this weekend.

One Palace player denied the opportunity to make an immediate impression is Jean-Philippe Mateta, who serves the second game of a three-match suspension following his straight red card in October's 2-0 defeat at Spurs.

Further concerns surround Ismaila Sarr (groin) and Jorgen Strand Larsen (ankle), who are doubtful for this weekend's encounter and could leave Frank without several match-winners.

While former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) is also touch-and-go for Saturday's match, Chadi Riad's knee injury will keep him sidelined until 2027.

Coventry City possible starting lineup:.

Rushworth; Van Ewijk, Mfuni, Pinnock, Dasilva; Torp, Grimes; Sakamoto, Rudoni, Gboho; Awoniyi.

Crystal Palace possible starting lineup:.

Henderson; Richards, Disasi, Lerma; Mingueza, Wharton, Timber, Mitchell; Kamada, Pino; Nketiah.

Frank's appointment should provide Palace with renewed purpose, but Mateta's suspension and doubts over Sarr and Strand Larsen leave the visitors short of attacking options.

Coventry have scored seven goals across their last three home matches and could exploit the Eagles' defensive uncertainty to spoil the Dane's first assignment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

In a recent development, arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

It has been revealed that arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

Arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

In a recent development, the visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

But Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

According to recent reports, london City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

According to recent reports, slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some new energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

Sources indicate that the Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

Industry observers note that rice has not just provided the presence and protection that Arsenal were hoping for with their £105 million signing. He has continued to develop his game, especially after returning to his deeper midfield role this season.

Rice has made the most line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, with Opta stats reported by Sky Sports showing he is second only to Premier League players.

While his running ability is still an asset, he is also becoming much better at penetrating through the defensive lines to find his teammates, giving Arsenal another option to move the ball forward with.

The development of Rice is key in securing a fresh contract at Arsenal.

The 27-year-old has already proven to be one of the most reliable members of Arteta’s squad and has shown great longevity by only missing five games out of his 119 Premier League outings in his first spell at the club.

Former West Ham teammate Jack Wilshere has also praised Rice’s strong work ethic, ability to adapt and natural leadership qualities.

Industry observers note that the reported 5-year deal will keep Rice at Arsenal until 2031, into his early 30s. While the terms of the deal have yet to be signed, it is a huge statement from the club.

They are not only rewarding Rice for what he has done but also investing in what he can do.

With Arteta finding latest ways to utilise Rice’s qualities in midfield, Rice could still have some of his best years ahead of him.

By Matthew Cooper | 19 Nov 2026 14:34.

Reading will be looking to get back to winning ways when they welcome Bromley to the Select Car Leasing Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit seventh in the League One table, while the visitors are rock bottom in 24th.

Reading will be looking for an immediate response after suffering a 3-1 defeat to fellow promotion contenders Stockport County last weekend.

Jack Marriott equalised for the Royals after Kyle Wootton had opened the scoring, but goals from Ethan Ennis and Jack Diamond ultimately earned an key victory for the Hatters.

That result saw Leam Richardson's side drop out of the playoff places, although they could return to the top six with a victory over Bromley if other results go their way.

Reading have now lost their last two league games, having also been beaten 2-0 by local rivals Oxford United, but they remain one of the most dangerous sides in the division.

The Royals have scored 26 goals in 15 league games so far, a number only eclipsed by four other teams, and the return of top scorer Marriott from injury has come as a welcome boost.

The veteran striker has scored in his last two games across all competitions and bagged a total of nine goals in 10 league games.

Bromley, meanwhile, have struggled to make the step up to League One and are bottom of the division with just nine points from 13 games.

The Ravens are without a win in their last 10 games across all competitions and new manager Karl Robinson says they "need to evolve" and "stick together" if they are to stay up this season.

Bromley's trip to Reading will be Robinson's first league game in charge, following a 2-0 defeat to Rotherham United in the FA Cup and a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons in the EFL Trophy.

It is worth noting that Bromley have never beaten Reading in a competitive fixture, although they did draw 1-1 in the EFL Cup earlier this season before the Royals triumphed on penalties.

Bromley form (all competitions):.

Reading will be able to welcome back Paudie O'Connor and Andy Rinomhota from suspension and they should come straight into the side.

Marriott is expected to lead the line, with support out wide from Kyreece Lisbie and Daniel Kyerewaa.

Victor Adeboyejo remains a doubt for Bromley after he suffered an injury in the warm-up ahead of the Rotherham game, meaning Michael Cheek is likely to start up front against Reading.

Jodi Jones and Mickel Miller are set to continue out wide, with George Saville and Kamil Conteh starting in midfield.

Pereira; Godwin-Malife, O'Connor, Knight, Roberts; Wing, Rinomhota; Lisbie, Savage, Kyerewaa; Marriott.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

Sources indicate that A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

Sources indicate that he was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

Storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Industry observers note that storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

He played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

According to recent reports, following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

Sources indicate that he will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium.
  • But doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.

Since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium. The Greek attacker scored 17 goals and made 23 assists in 36 league games.

But doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League. In his first stint in England with Norwich City, he revealed little sign of becoming the player he is now.

Sources indicate that since making his debut for the club, Tzolis has become a more rounded attacking threat. He has started all 7 Premier League games this season and provides a reliable option on the left for Arteta.

However, in recent comments, it seems that he is aware of the perceptions around his physicality and is keen to change them.

Tzolis spoke to Arsenal Media, saying that he doesn’t think the notion of him lacking the physicality to play at top level has validity.

Recent findings suggest that he claimed that he is not a player without muscle and cited his accomplishments. He also described his tendency to use aggression against his opponents.

According to recent reports, this is a key part of Arteta’s system at the club. Tzolis is expected to press from the flanks if Arsenal lose the ball.

Industry observers note that tzolis is comfortable with this role. He is able to track back well to support his full-back, adding an extra dimension to the left side.

The Greek international has proven his physical ability outside of match play. He was nicknamed Leonidas by the fitness team at the club due to a strong performance in pre-season.

It is reported that he completed the running challenge better than anyone in the squad.

Tzolis has joined Arsenal to add attacking flair to the squad, having left for Besiktas. He looks like he could be a formidable goalscorer and creator.

In the league last season, Tzolis contributed 40 goals and put in a good performance in Europe. This led to Arsenal spending a reported £34 million to bring him to the club.

He has not had the best impact in the league, registering just one assist and no goals, but this should not be taken to mean he is not contributing.

Tzolis has shown an ability to fit into Arteta’s style of play. His defensive contribution, work rate and combative nature may prove very valuable in tough away games.

Despite there being plenty to improve on, Tzolis provides more than just an attacking option for Arsenal.

If Tzolis can change people’s view of him in terms of his physicality and continues to put his technical skills and determination together, then he can be a valuable asset in Arteta’s looks.

Max Dowman shortly returns to action for Arsenal after serving a three-game suspension.

His absence has been disappointing, but the experience should give the youngster an key lesson. Can he put the incident behind him and show Mikel Arteta that he can be trusted?

Industry observers note that dowman was sent off in an unfortunate moment. He was heavily challenged by Neal and, after lashing out, was shown a straight red card.

Although this one moment should not be enough to dismiss a young player from the game completely, it can serve as a valuable lesson on the pressure that comes with playing at a higher level.

Industry observers note that opponents will test Dowman physically, but he must learn to keep his composure. As he starts making an impact, some players may target his age and inexperience to unsettle him.

As he gets more game time, consistency will be key. Arteta must be confident that Dowman can be relied on in high pressure situations.

Arsenal do not need to rush Dowman into the first team. The squad’s quality allows Arteta to manage his minutes and give him time to develop without putting too much pressure on him.

If Dowman is to play against Manchester City, it will depend on Arteta’s prepares, but he has certainly done enough to warrant consideration.

The suspension should not define his season. What matters now is how he responds, both on and off the pitch.

Dowman has the talent to become an vital player for Arsenal. Keeping his discipline will be just as important as displaying his ability.

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 14:43.

Barcelona have reportedly earmarked Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and two other defenders as transfer targets ahead of the January window.

Hansi Flick's men have enjoyed an excellent start to the 2026-27 campaign on the domestic scene, winning 11 of their opening 12 top-flight contests, meaning that they sit top of the La Liga standings.

Barca have been linked heavily to upcoming defensive additions in recent times, including Tottenham Hotspur man Pedro Perro, however, it is believed that the Catalans are not pursuing a deal for the World Cup winner in the New Year.

Head coach Flick is supposedly targeting the signing of a centre-back and a full-back during the upcoming trading point, aiming to strengthen his side's chances of winning the Champions League for the first time since 2015.

Hoping to record four consecutive competitive victories, Barcelona welcome Europe-chasing Villarreal to Camp Nou on Sunday afternoon, when club action will return following the international break.

As per Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, Barcelona will press forward in their search for a latest defender during the January transfer window, in which head coach Flick is expected to be backed by sporting director Deco.

The report claims that Barca are keen on the cost-effective option of bringing Manchester United centre-back Martinez to the club, with the 2022 World Cup winner approaching the end of his contract at Old Trafford.

As well as the outspoken United star, it is understood that the La Liga leaders are also eyeing up a move for Borussia Dortmund's Nico Schlotterbeck, who is capable of playing at centre-back and left-back.

The 26-year-old was given his senior Germany debut by Barca boss Flick in March 2022, and the Dortmund sweetheart is supposedly available for £50m ahead of the winter transfer window.

Finally, it is believed that Barca's hierarchy are yet to shelve the possibility of signing Inter Milan and Italy defender Alessandro Bastoni, who is noted to be open to a La Liga switch amid a £33m valuation.

After his explosive comments following defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, Martinez created a major rift between himself and the Manchester United board, as well as former head coach Carrick.

The general consensus is that the 28-year-old's time at Old Trafford is up, and it would be surprising if the Red Devils triggered the extension clause in the defender's current contract.

That being remarked, the arrival of compatriot Mauricio Pochettino could hand Martinez a second chance this season, with the centre-back potentially playing himself back into favour at the Theatre of Dreams.

#15182. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

📅 30 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4848 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.
  • Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five.
  • But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”.

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

Sources indicate that “After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso mentioned. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”.

Industry observers note that it is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl.

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez stated. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

According to recent reports, conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Recent findings suggest that caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was rapidly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”.

Chelsea’s latest set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

According to recent reports, macPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

Industry observers note that fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they revealed it in certain moments of the game.”.

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro claims he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert.

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D.

September 5: Brighton vs Leeds (Premier League)September 13: Coventry vs Brighton (Premier League)September 16: Manchester United vs Brighton (League Cup)September 19: Brighton vs Arsenal (Premier League)October 10: Sunderland vs Brighton (Premier League).

September 6: Arsenal vs Chelsea (Premier League)September 9: Chelsea vs Leeds (League Cup)September 12: Chelsea vs Hull (Premier League)September 18: Brentford vs Chelsea (Premier League)October 10: Chelsea vs Bournemouth (Premier League).

The final game of the day comes from the north west as Manchester United host newly-promoted Ipswich. That game kicks off at 4.30pm and you can follow all the live action from that match right here.

Chelsea 4 Brighton 3 Leeds 1 Brentford 1 Sunderland 1 Fulham 0.

Possession: Chelsea 26%-74% BrightonShots: 17-15Shots on target: 6-6Corners: 4-7Touches in opposition box: 29-28.

There is no time for Brighton to push for the equaliser as the final whistle is blown at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea make it two wins from two to start the new Premier League season but were pushed all the way by Brighton. It finishes 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

Industry observers note that it could well be the last touch of the game but Brighton have a small amount of hope as Gross heads past Martinez. If that had come a few minutes ago, maybe Brighton could have pushed for a draw.

Brighton have a corner and if they are to have any chance of potentially rescuing a point, they have to score right now. De Cuyper’s inswinger is clipped into a dangerous area but for some odd reason referee Michael Oliver gives Chelsea a free-kick. Absolutely ridiculous decision; there was no foul in any way, shape or form.

Industry observers note that chelsea look to counter through Pedro, who is then brought down by Costinha. It is an easy booking for referee Michael Oliver to give.

Sources indicate that how many added minutes will there be? The answer is five minutes.

Boscagli is booked for bringing down Rogers.

This is a concern for Chelsea as Caicedo, who came on as a second-half substitute, is now having to go off injured. In his place is former Brighton man Barco, who slapped Bellingham at the World Cup. Barco is booed vociferously by the travelling Brighton fans.

Meanwhile Leeds are level 1-1 against Brentford at Elland Road thanks to Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser.

Double change for Brighton as Costinha and David replace Wieffer and Kostoulas.

Brighton scored four a week ago against Aston Villa on the opening weekend but have conceded four this weekend. If they can get a goal though soon, it would make the home fans inside Stamford Bridge very nervous.

Kadioglu has an effort from the edge of the Chelsea box but drags his effort wide.

Meanwhile, up in the north east, Isidor has put Sunderland 1-0 up against Fulham at the Stadium of Light.

Palmer has been pretty quiet today but Chelsea’s two-goal lead is restored. He receives it from Pedro and drives forward through the Brighton half. As he approaches the edge of the penalty area, Palmer calmly slots home into the bottom corner.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

Tuchel will have like that. He may not have had a brilliant game, but Palmer just scored a brilliant goal. That should be enough for Chelsea.

Fabian Hurzeler turns to his bench for the first time today as Osman comes on for Yalcouye, who was impressive.

Xabi Alonso turns to his bench again as Chavarria replaces Colwill.

We have this news from the Premier League:.

In a recent development, #CHEBHAMatch Officials are operating in the second half without communications packs due to an ongoing technical concern. VAR remains in operation via a back-up system using messages sent to the referee's watch and radio communication to the fourth official if required.

It has been revealed that dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

According to recent reports, chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

Recent findings suggest that it is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

It has been revealed that this game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a big deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

It has been revealed that gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

England head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea have two substantial chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

It has been revealed that arsenal are looking to strengthen their attacking options in January. One player they are reportedly keeping an eye on is Brentford winger Kevin Schade. Mikel Arteta will be keen to add competition in attack, and Schade may be a good option.

Schade will give additional pace to the offence. He is capable of playing in multiple attacking positions to provide Arteta with extra depth in the squad.

However, it may be difficult to get Schade. He is on loan at Brentford, and may want to keep him in the long term. If Schade is seen as a key player in the future, they may be difficult to negotiate with.

Schade’s versatility is another major plus. His speed and straightforward method make him hard to deal with for defenders. In addition, he can be used as a left-sided attacker, giving Arteta more flexibility in his front line. As the club are playing in a number of competitions, this can be very useful.

Schade has already scored 3 times in the Premier League this season. He has rapidly adapted to playing in England after moving from Freiburg to Brentford in 2023.

Despite only being 24 years old, Schade still has a lot to improve on. He has lots of experience in the Premier League but has not quite reached the peak of his ability yet. If he moves to Arsenal, he may be able to elevate his performance.

Brentford has already started negotiations with Schade regarding a contract extension that would keep him tied to the club for a long time. He is already contracted until the summer of 2028.

Arsenal’s interest could prove problematic. Other clubs are also keeping their eyes on this player. Tottenham in particular are not seen as a major threat at this stage.

It is going to be very challenging for Brentford to let go of Schade because he has played a key part in their offensive setup, and losing Schade could prove disastrous.

Arsenal will have to pay Brentford whatever they ask for, Schade, and since he has a decent amount of time left on his contract, Brentford has an edge in negotiations.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal’s interest in Schade is logical. His versatility will provide Arteta with additional flexibility because of his prior experience in the Premier League.

Sources indicate that it can be considered positive to sign fresh strikers. Arsenal must decide if they believe that Schade will fit in well with their current players and whether the asking price from Brentford is reasonable.

As of now, there are no signs of a transfer on the horizon, but it is clear that Schade is a player worth monitoring as the winter transfer window approaches.

The boyish, Lego-obsessed son of a farmer who quit Man City to become England's No 1: How James Trafford - with £95m spent on him - is maturing to star for Leeds and the Three Lions

  • In a recent development, 'It was like meeting a kid at a sixth-form careers day'.
  • When, at England's World Cup base in Kansas City, I then sat down with Trafford and he revealed that his partner had packed some Lego for him to build in camp, you wondered if sixth-form was a grade too high.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:35 EST, 16 November 2026.

In a recent development, 'It was like meeting a kid at a sixth-form careers day'. That was the verdict, slightly unflattering but endearing all the same, of one Premier League chief after encountering James Trafford.

When, at England's World Cup base in Kansas City, I then sat down with Trafford and he revealed that his partner had packed some Lego for him to build in camp, you wondered if sixth-form was a grade too high.

He is the son of a Cumbrian farmer and the Lego was of a tractor, which he would save for later in the tournament. 'You don't want to go too early,' he stated.

In a recent development, none of this is a criticism. Far from it. There was a boyish charm, an innocence, even, and Trafford was engaging tech giant. Nonetheless, he did not sound ready for the likes of a World Cup semi-final against Argentina. Thomas Tuchel agreed.

Recent findings suggest that but every boy will one day become a man. On a ferocious and febrile night in Madrid, no place for adolescents, we may just have witnessed James Trafford's graduation ceremony.

Sources indicate that without his double save in stoppage-time, England would have left Spain without a famous, and deserved, victory. One Spanish title labelled it 'la actuacion de su vida', the performance of his life. You wonder how much they saw of his loan spell at Accrington Stanley, but the sentiment stands.

James Trafford celebrates with Jarell Quansah, Dan Burn and Ezri Konsa during his starring performance in Spain.

Trafford pictured with his farmer father, David, in the cab of his tractor with their dogs (Source: James Trafford).

Madrid daily AS exclaimed: 'Magisterio de Trafford!' Translated, 'A Trafford Masterclass!'. They claim he was the reason Spain could not complete their comeback, and they would be right.

When Tuchel stood with us in a corridor of the Metropolitano Stadium on the eve of the game, he had no problem confirming that Trafford would start. His message, though, was clear - it was sink or swim for a goalkeeper who turned 24 last month.

Sources indicate that not only did Trafford keep his head above water, it was he who pulled the team ashore. It was he to whom his senior colleagues ran in celebration. Ezri Konsa nearly took the shirt off Trafford's back, such was the force of his gratitude. But maybe this was the occasion when Trafford took the No 1 jersey from the back of Jordan Pickford, the holder for nearly a decade.

Pickford has done nothing wrong. Were Trafford to still display that maturity deficit, Pickford would be a reliable custodian heading to Euro 2028. This is not Peter Shilton post Italia 90, an uncomfortable truth of a great in need of the retirement barn. The 32-year-old has plenty to give on the back of all he has already given.

This, admitted Tuchel after the 3-2 win, is a selection dilemma that allows a manager to sleep well at night.

'There is no headache at all!' he boomed. 'I'm so far away from a headache, I cannot imagine.

Trafford left Manchester City with the initiative to usurp Jordan Pickford as England No 1.

Jude Bellingham certainly seemed impressed with the performance of the goalkeeper.

'This is what we wanted. This is the best thing that can happen to all of us, also to Pickers. It is amazing how they push each other, and if then Traff has a performance like this, he has it because he knows he's well prepared. He gets the push from his colleagues and competitors.'.

It has been revealed that tuchel has seen enough of Trafford in training and around camp to believe he is ready for promotion. He has watched him for Leeds, where he rates as the best performing goalkeeper in the Premier League. His 'net goals prevented' (4.4) and 'save percentage' (81.4) are higher than any rival this season, including Pickford.

Industry observers note that 'You always have to deserve your place,' added Tuchel. 'You will never get a gift and just get a game (for the sake of it). So he deserved to play and we expected this kind of performance. It was not only the last save, but also the build-up play and not losing focus. He has proved it on this stage, so this gives him a lot of belief. Now, it's on him to keep going for it.'.

It, you presume, is the No 1 jersey. Trafford has made no secret of his desire to take it from Pickford, and he told us in the summer that such ambition was the motivation behind him wanting to leave Manchester City for a second time.

That day, he flipped his room key with a magician's sleight of hand throughout the interview, a dexterity useful for Lego. Better still for fingertip saves such as the one to deny Aymeric Laporte in the 91st minute.

Also in the gift pack from his girlfriend were two face masks. 'Very thoughtful,' he quipped. But that is another observation, bordering on concern, that some prospective buyers have made in recent years - on the goalkeeping scale of uber professional to joker, he resides too close to the latter. We have seen, even this season, the odd concentration lapse that speaks to that thought.

Trafford has played a starring role in goal since moving to Leeds United in the summer.

Industry observers note that but there was also a feeling that Trafford needed more exposure and responsibility before the penny dropped and his value was realised. Already, £95million has been spent on him in transfer fees.

According to recent reports, at Leeds, and now with England, he has been given that stage, as Tuchel calls it. The head coach maintains that Pickford is his first choice, but it was Trafford he picked for both Nations League fixtures against Spain, the ones that really mattered, the ones that would strengthen or threaten his own employment.

As for Trafford's career prospects, to revisit our opening line, England's No 1 sounds like a fair vocation.

Thomas Tuchel wants England to use victory in the Nations League finals as a springboard to winning Euro 2028 at Wembley.

The head coach admits it has taken him a while to recover from the trauma of his side’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July, for which he was heavily criticised.

But after beating world champions Spain 3-2 on Sunday night, topping their Nations League group ahead of March’s quarter-finals and next summer's finals, Tuchel is finally able to look forward with positivity and belief.

‘I saw the celebrations in Portugal when they won the Nations League,’ he mentioned. ‘It’s just the best, the best preparation we can have for the Euros. We want to have these matches on the highest level to prove ourselves and to gain confidence, to see where we are and to adjust our game where we need to, that’s what this Nations League is perfect for. We want to win it.’.

In a recent development, england have won five of their six matches since the World Cup, losing only to Spain at Wembley in September. In the build up to that game, Tuchel was involved in heated exchanges with observers who continued to question his tactics in the final half hour against Argentina.

’It took me a while to digest (the World Cup exit) and see the way forward, how we can help and adjust and improve, and how we can do this together,’ he stated.

Sources indicate that ‘We had reviews and so on, but clarity then came together with the players. Straight away we had the energy right to take the next steps. The ideas became more clear for me, even if it was not so easy the first week, to overcome and arrive with different emotions. Some were still upset from the World Cup. Some were newly introduced in the team. Some had digested it, some had not digested it. But it was important to have this kind of process together.

According to recent reports, ‘(Spain) was a complete performance that makes me very proud. It's a full package of belief, of courage, of commitment, of togetherness, of relying on each other and stepping up in this moment.’.

Tuchel, though, has rejected the idea that seeing out the win Madrid was proof that he has learned from his mistakes in Atlanta.

‘Not at all, I think we would not have been in this situation if it was 11 against 11,’ he said. ‘For me, it was Mexico reloaded (not Argentina). It's one man down, but what can you do? It is their strength to have ball possession, to overload and find the gaps. It just plays totally into their hands and it comes wave after wave. It felt like three hours and thirty minutes!’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 14:47, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:19.
  • Returning to action following the final international break of the year, St Mirren make the short journey to Celtic on Saturday looking for a victory that could draw them level on points with the teams in the top half of the Scottish Premiership.
  • The Bhoys entered the break with a return to winning ways in the league courtesy of a narrow 1-0 victory over bottom-placed Kilmarnock, while the Buddies suffered their second consecutive defeat with a home loss to Rangers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 14:47, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:19.

Returning to action following the final international break of the year, St Mirren make the short journey to Celtic on Saturday looking for a victory that could draw them level on points with the teams in the top half of the Scottish Premiership.

The Bhoys entered the break with a return to winning ways in the league courtesy of a narrow 1-0 victory over bottom-placed Kilmarnock, while the Buddies suffered their second consecutive defeat with a home loss to Rangers.

After securing a record-extending 56th Scottish top-flight title on a dramatic final day of the season in May, Celtic began the 2026-27 campaign hoping for more of the same, retaining Martin O'Neill as manager, and he will take charge of his 339th game at the helm this weekend.

While they right now sit top of the Scottish Premiership with a four-point cushion over arch-rivals Rangers, their season has been far from straightforward, with the Bhoys entering the international break having recorded just one league victory in their previous three outings.

A home draw against Dundee United was followed by a defeat away to Falkirk, their first loss to the Bairns in nearly two decades, before they were presented with an opportunity to return to winning ways against basement side Kilmarnock, although their eventual 1-0 victory was far from convincing.

O'Neill's side took the lead through Republic of Ireland international Liam Scales but were made to work hard for all three points against a team that has won just twice all season.

Celtic have struggled even more in Europe, with just one victory from their opening four Europa League matches leaving them 32nd in the 36-team league phase and facing an uphill battle to reach the knockout stages.

Meanwhile, St Mirren have endured a difficult spell since their 2-1 defeat to Celtic in September, losing seven of their subsequent nine league matches and collecting fewer points than any other side in the division during that period, although their early-season results have at least kept them clear of the bottom two.

Led by Craig McLeish, who took charge on a permanent basis in June, the Buddies have won four, drawn two and lost seven of their opening 13 league fixtures, with the teams below them potentially able to close the gap through games in hand.

While they secured a narrow victory over Dundee in October, St Mirren have collected just one point from their subsequent three top-flight outings, extending their disappointing run of form.

The appointment of a young manager with ambitions of introducing a progressive style of football has yet to produce the desired results, with the Buddies' 12 goals scored representing the joint-lowest total in the division, while their 22 conceded is the second-highest.

After beating Kilmarnock 1-0 in early September, St Mirren sat second in the table with 10 points from a possible 12, but collecting just four more across their next nine matches has brought their promising start to a halt, although that early form provides a platform for McLeish's side to build on if they can rediscover their confidence.

Celtic Scottish Premiership form:.

Celtic form (all competitions):.

St Mirren Scottish Premiership form:.

Unlike their upcoming opponents, Celtic had several players away on international duty over the past fortnight and may need to make changes depending on their fitness following the additional travel.

Auston Trusty recently took a break from football following the death of his father and has not featured for O'Neill's side since their 4-1 Europa League defeat to Benfica in October.

However, he scored for the USA against Haiti during the international break and dedicated his goal to his father, potentially putting himself in contention for a return this weekend.

Alistair Johnston would have travelled to North America to join up with the Canada squad but remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained during a 2-1 victory over Hibernian at the end of October.

The Canadian full-back and German midfielder Mika Baur are O'Neill's only expected absentees, although it remains to be seen whether Kasper Hogh will retain his place up front after failing to score for the 16th consecutive match last time out.

As for St Mirren, they could name the same starting XI for a second consecutive match, although McLeish may be tempted to make changes following the two-week break.

Nikolas Agrafiotis, Malik Dijksteel and Keanu Baccus have all been sidelined through injury but are expected to return in the coming weeks, with Saturday potentially coming too soon for some of the trio.

Jonah Ayunga is also unavailable through injury and is not expected to return until early 2027.

Celtic possible starting lineup:.

Johnstone; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; McGregor, Baur; Duran, Nygren, Jota; Hogh.

St Mirren possible starting lineup:.

Chapman; Fraser, Gogic, Jackson; Ramsay, Phillips, Taylor, John; Ramos, Young, Kabia.

The division's highest scorers come up against its least productive attack this weekend, and we expect that gulf in quality to be reflected at Celtic Park.

Celtic should have enough to secure a second consecutive league victory, extending their lead over St Mirren and maintaining at least a four-point cushion over Rangers heading into the following weekend.
