German Giants Eye West Ham Star But Face £22m Obstacle

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham United midfielder Arne Engels is attracting interest from Bundesliga side VfB Stuttgart, although the German club could struggle to afford the £22m summer signing.
  • According to German newspaper BILD, as reported by Sport Witness, Stuttgart have identified Engels as one of several potential replacements for Angelo Stiller, who could leave the club next summer.
  • However, Stuttgart reportedly regard the cost of signing Engels as unrealistic, with West Ham unlikely to accept a substantial loss on a player who only arrived from Celtic in August.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United midfielder Arne Engels is attracting interest from Bundesliga side VfB Stuttgart, although the German club could struggle to afford the £22m summer signing.

According to German newspaper BILD, as reported by Sport Witness, Stuttgart have identified Engels as one of several potential replacements for Angelo Stiller, who could leave the club next summer. Southampton’s Caspar Jander and Middlesbrough’s Aidan Morris are also under consideration.

However, Stuttgart reportedly regard the cost of signing Engels as unrealistic, with West Ham unlikely to accept a substantial loss on a player who only arrived from Celtic in August. The German club previously wanted the Belgian during his time at Augsburg, so this is not an entirely fresh interest.

Look, clearly Engels is somebody that West Ham head of recruitment Nils Koppen values extremely highly.

Industry observers note that as we reported when the £22m agreement with Celtic was reached, the Belgian had been Koppen’s primary midfield target throughout much of the summer. West Ham pursued him for weeks before finally getting their man.

I thought very promptly he’d become one of the first names on the team sheet under Nuno Espírito Santo, and I suspect that will continue under Scott Parker.

So clearly he is a player who is admired.

That said, I’m not surprised Stuttgart are struggling to find value at £22m because I do think West Ham overpaid when we bought him from Celtic.

West Ham midfielders will play with more freedom under Parker which could unlock Engels value.

Industry observers note that now, that price becomes fully justified if he helps get the team promoted this season. If not, then I’d have to say that so far he’s done little to justify the price tag.

Sources indicate that that’s not to suggest Engels is a bad player. He’s a busy, high-energy midfielder who covers plenty of ground and contributes to the team’s overall play.

But there’s a difference between being a good Championship midfielder and looking like a £22m player.

Indeed, when I recently assessed Koppen’s summer recruitment, Engels was one of the players I felt remained something of an unknown quantity in terms of value for money.

But, and here’s the crucial thing, West Ham manager Scott Parker has a habit of getting central midfielders scoring goals.

And if he can get Engels further up the pitch than Nuno Espírito Santo managed to, and into goalscoring positions, I suspect his value will rise if he becomes a goalscorer rather than just a busy, high-energy midfield player.

We’ve already had a glimpse of what might be possible.

Engels scored his first West Ham goal during the extraordinary 3-3 draw at Cardiff City in Parker’s opening match, as the Hammers recovered from three goals down at half-time.

That was one of the positives from a remarkable second-half performance, which I discussed in my player ratings following the Cardiff comeback.

According to recent reports, however, against Blackburn, Parker used Engels in a deeper midfield role, with Mohamadou Kanté and Divine Mukasa operating further forward. As our Blackburn match report highlighted, that arrangement helped protect the defence but offered Engels fewer opportunities to get forward.

It will be interesting to see whether Parker can find a balance between the two.

Engels has the energy to get around the pitch, and if he can add regular goals to his game, the argument over whether West Ham paid too much could begin to look very different.

For now, Stuttgart’s interest looks more like an indication of Engels’ standing in the game than an immediate threat to West Ham.

The Belgian is under contract until 2031, with the club holding an option for another year, as confirmed by West Ham’s official website.

And with the Hammers attempting to win promotion at the first attempt, I can’t imagine Koppen being particularly enthusiastic about losing the player he worked so hard to sign.

Personally, I still believe £22m was too much money for what Engels has shown us so far.

But if Parker can turn him into a midfielder who regularly arrives in the penalty area and contributes goals, that assessment could change considerably.

And if those goals help West Ham get promoted, nobody will be complaining about the transfer fee.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48.
  • Genclerbirligi will be looking to return to winning ways when they welcome Gaziantep to Eryaman Stadium on Saturday afternoon in the Turkish Super Lig.
  • The hosts sit 14th in the table with 11 points from as many matches, three points clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors are 16th and in the drop zone with eight points after losing seven of their opening 11 league fixtures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48.

Genclerbirligi will be looking to return to winning ways when they welcome Gaziantep to Eryaman Stadium on Saturday afternoon in the Turkish Super Lig.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 11 points from as many matches, three points clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors are 16th and in the drop zone with eight points after losing seven of their opening 11 league fixtures.

Genclerbirligi head into Saturday's encounter after suffering a 3-0 defeat away to Besiktas in their last league outing, having been unable to build on the confidence gained from their emphatic 5-0 victory over Alanyaspor a week earlier.

That win was their biggest of the campaign and followed another 5-0 success against Karakopru Belediyespor in the Turkish Cup, but their return to league action in Istanbul brought them back down to earth as Besiktas scored twice before half-time and added a third after the break.

The Red-and-Blacks have now lost three of their last four league matches and won just one of their last nine, with their only victory during that period coming against Alanyaspor, while they have conceded 21 goals in 11 league fixtures, the third-highest total in the division.

Their defensive record has been a particular concern away from home, where they have conceded 14 times in five matches and scored just once, although their performances in Ankara have generally been more encouraging.

Genclerbirligi have collected eight points from six home league matches, winning twice, drawing twice and losing twice, and they have scored nine goals at Eryaman Stadium in the competition, with their 2-1 victory over Fenerbahce representing the highlight.

Bernd Storck's side will hope to avoid another winless streak by bouncing back immediately, with optimism stemming from their home results and the fact that they beat the visitors on this ground in their last meeting here, while they have also never lost to them at home (W4, D1).

Gaziantep, meanwhile, have endured a much more difficult spell, losing their last six league matches and failing to score in each of their most recent two outings.

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has admitted that Alphonse Areola is unlikely to be available for Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, leaving the Hammers with a familiar goalkeeping dilemma.

Speaking during his pre-match press conference, Parker explained that the club had attempted to push the Frenchman’s recovery but were struggling to get him ready.

“We tried to push it a bit, but it looks a little bit unlikely and we’ll leave it as long as we can before making a decision,” stated the West Ham boss.

This isn’t particularly surprising. It’s something we’ve discussed previously on Claret & Hugh, with concerns surrounding Areola’s match fitness and reports that he has been carrying too much weight.

And considering Parker has worked with the Frenchman before, one has to assume he’d be really keen to play him.

The fact that he isn’t selecting Areola suggests the goalkeeper simply isn’t ready for action, particularly following his recent injury setback.

Personally, my choice would be to give young Fin Herrick a chance.

I was speaking to my Hammers Chat counterpart Geo during our West Ham v Preston preview this week, and he made an excellent observation.

The one thing Mads Hermansen has consistently been good at is his distribution with the ball at his feet.

Unfortunately, his clanger for Denmark in their last game means even that aspect of his performances is now under scrutiny.

He’s got the yips: West Ham goalkeeper Mads Hermansen, whose recent performances have raised concerns about his confidence.

I actually think the best thing we could possibly do for Hermansen would be to give him a rest.

His confidence has clearly taken a battering, and his latest international mistake has only increased the pressure.

Let’s be fair, young Herrick can’t perform any worse than the Danish keeper has in the last few games.

And as our recent coverage of supporters’ goalkeeping preferences demonstrated, there is already considerable dissatisfaction with the current situation.

I appreciate throwing a youngster into such an important game carries risks, but there comes a point when continuing with an out-of-form goalkeeper becomes an equally significant gamble.

For me, Saturday presents an opportunity to try something different.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has spoken positively about Joël Piroe ahead of Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, raising an interesting question over his starting striker.

During his pre-match press conference, Parker acknowledged the Dutchman’s impressive goalscoring record and revealed that he was looking forward to spending more time working with him.

Industry observers note that “I’ve known about Joël, having played against his teams. His goalscoring record is really good,” said Parker.

“It’s a shame for us he’s been away, but he’s in good form, and I’m looking forward to working with him more.”.

Personally, I would 100% start Piroe ahead of Taty Castellanos, irrespective of how well the Argentine might have trained during the international break.

Piroe is a proven Championship goalscorer, and Parker knows all about him from his previous experience managing in this division.

I think he very much deserves a run of games in an attempt to fire at least one of our strikers into action.

The alternative is to continue persevering with Castellanos, who has been a considerable disappointment since West Ham’s relegation.

And there is another factor to consider.

As Claret & Hugh exclusively revealed, the club are exploring the possibility of selling Castellanos in January, with Nils Koppen already investigating potential replacements.

Further reports from Argentina have suggested the striker wants to leave, although no departure has been agreed.

Piroe is admired by Scott Parker.

I don’t think there’s any mystery surrounding what Piroe offers.

He knows the Championship, he knows how to score goals in it, and he’s already demonstrated that he can contribute to this West Ham team.

As we’ve previously argued when discussing Parker’s selection options, Piroe has a compelling case to start ahead of Castellanos.

Of course, the manager will have his own ideas about how he wants his centre-forward to play.

But given the lack of goals from our recognised strikers, I’d rather see Parker give the Dutchman a proper opportunity than continue waiting for Castellanos to discover some form.

For me, Piroe starts against Preston.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:49, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:30.

Galatasaray will aim to stretch their lead at the top of the Turkish Super Lig table when they host struggling Samsunspor on Saturday afternoon.

The match has been moved from RAMS Park because of pitch problems and will now be played at Basaksehir Fatih Terim Stadium, with the league leaders given extra time to carry out maintenance and improvement work ahead of their upcoming UEFA Champions League fixture against Aston Villa.

Galatasaray went into the international break on a six-game winning streak in all competitions, a run that began with a 1-0 victory over Genclerbirligi before they beat Lille 4-2 in the Champions League and Fenerbahce 2-1 at home in the league.

The Lions then won 4-0 away to Konyaspor, beat Stuttgart 2-0 in the Champions League and edged Amedspor 4-3 just before the break, with their attacking output particularly impressive as they scored at least twice in five of those six matches.

In the victory over Amed, Galatasaray raced into a 3-0 lead through Rafael Leao's early strike, an own goal from goalkeeper Alban Lafont and Alexey Batrakov's effort before the hour mark, but they subsequently conceded twice before Baris Alper Yilmaz restored their two-goal cushion in the 80th minute, only for the hosts to concede again in stoppage time before holding on for the victory.

Okan Buruk's side have suffered just one league defeat this season, a 4-0 loss away to Trabzonspor, which has left them with 28 points from 11 matches, having also drawn 2-2 at home against Corum in their opening game of the campaign.

Keeping opponents off the scoresheet at home has been an concern for Cimbom, who have conceded in five of their six home league matches this season, including each of their last three.

Samsunspor won the last meeting against Galatasaray to end a nine-game losing streak in this fixture, but the visitors arrive in considerably worse form this season.

However, they received a much-needed boost just before the break, beating Konyaspor 1-0 at home to end an eight-game winless streak, which had been a club record.

It was also the first victory under Nenad Bjelica, who was appointed in October to replace Thorsten Fink, who was dismissed after nine months in charge following just one win in his opening seven matches.

Samsunspor are 17th on seven points, one place above the bottom and one point from safety, and while they finally recorded some positivity before the break, they travel to a venue where they have lost eight consecutive games, leaving them with a difficult task after the international hiatus.

Galatasaray form (all competitions):.

Samsunspor Turkish Super Lig form:.

Galatasaray have major absentees, with Victor Osimhen undergoing surgery on a loose fragment in his left knee after the Stuttgart game and expected to be out for several weeks.

Leao is also sidelined through injury, while goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir picked up a shoulder problem on international duty and is not expected to play, with Gunay Guvenc tipped to start between the posts.

Davinson Sanchez is also unavailable after withdrawing from Colombia's squad with a muscle problem, while Roland Sallai is sidelined through injury and Batrakov is also listed as unavailable.

Samsunspor have fewer concerns, although Celil Yuksel is sidelined through injury and Fatih Kaya remains a doubt.

Mohamed Bayo is expected to lead the attack, with Tanguy Coulibaly, Oskar Ohlenschlæger and Afonso Sousa providing support from the attacking midfield positions.

Galatasaray possible starting lineup:.

Gunay; Singo, Bardakci, Jakobs, Elmali; Torreira, Lemina; Akgun, Sara, Sane; Yilmaz.

Samsunspor possible starting lineup:.

Bayazit; Mendes, Erakovic, Drapinski, Tomasson; Watt, Onur; Coulibaly, Ohlenschlæger, Sousa; Bayo.

Galatasaray are without their main striker, first-choice goalkeeper and Leao, but they still possess considerably greater squad depth and arrive in strong form, which should prove too much for Samsunspor as we expect the league leaders to secure a comfortable victory.

Man United's first woman on their backroom team, the fitness enforcer, a scorpion-kicking goalkeeper coach... and his son! Meet Mauricio Pochettino's team of experts flying in to whip United's flops into shape

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1767 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.
  • The Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.

The Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone. With him, Pochettino brings to Old Trafford an experienced and familiar cast of trusted colleagues, who will be tasked with supporting him in his mission to turn things around in Manchester.

From a first-team coach who has known him since 1992 to the boss' own son, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the backroom staff accompanying Pochettino at United...

Sources indicate that when the Manchester United reporters turn up for press conferences at Carrington, they will notice one seat, usually in the front row and to the far left, has a reserved sign on it. It will be for Perez, who is Pochettino’s eyes and ears. Those same correspondents may well be followed by Perez on social media, so he can stay in the loop of what is being written.

Recent findings suggest that wherever Pochettino goes, so too does his shadow Perez. You have probably already heard about the time Pochettino met his idol Sir Alex Ferguson for lunch in London back in 2016. What you may not know is that Perez was there, too. He and Pochettino have been joined at the hip ever since they met in Barcelona when one was an analyst and the other was managing Espanyol.

Mauricio Pochettino (right) arrives at Manchester United with a trusted team of backroom staff.

That was in 2010. Perez had studied sports science at university and completed his coaching qualifications but was considering quitting football. Pochettino convinced him otherwise, and they soon learned they shared the same principles, including the importance of creating the right culture of togetherness within a club to succeed.

In 2013, it was Perez’s turn to convince Pochettino. The Argentinian was unsure about moving to England to manage Southampton, but the Spaniard had spent a month on these shores studying how Premier League sides train and play.

He told Pochettino that the intensity of his sessions and style would fit perfectly and that he could not turn down the chance to take on the Premier League.

According to recent reports, they now consider each other family, and Perez’s story itself is a nice one. By his own admission, he will tell you he failed at becoming a professional player, but he believes the way in which he worked his way in as a coach can inspire others who dream of finding their own place in football.

It has been revealed that he loves the game, so much so that he would use days off to travel from London to Manchester to visit the National Football Museum. Now he will be living much closer to his favourite hotspot.

As well as being the glue which connects various club departments together, Perez is a fitness and conditioning specialist, and a normal working day might involve him arriving at the training ground at 7.30am.

Sources indicate that after meeting with Pochettino over breakfast, he will then hold a 9am medical meeting where plans for each player are discussed and decided. Programmes tend to be tailored to individuals rather than set for the whole squad. Perez was credited with helping to establish Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur as among the fittest teams in the Premier League.

Where Pochettino is larger than life, Perez is unassuming, and has never sought to step into management as he prefers to work in the shadows.

Jesus Perez, pictured with Pochettino at Spurs in 2019, has long been his right-hand man.

We talk about Pochettino’s man-management prowess, but the same is true of Perez.

For example, when Chelsea beat Leicester City 4-2 in an FA Cup quarter-final in 2023-24, Raheem Sterling had a stinker. He missed a penalty, spurned a one-on-one and skied a free-kick. Chelsea’s fans booed him, and chanted ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ at Pochettino when he substituted Mykhailo Mudryk rather than Sterling after 78 minutes at 2-2. Perez was the first to go straight to Sterling to put an arm around him that day.

And when Cole Palmer was becoming a household name in Pochettino’s one and only season at Chelsea, Perez was among those who privately tried to help the Englishman understand the perils of the distractions of his newly introduced-found fame.

When they departed Chelsea, Pochettino and Perez were men of their word and honoured their commitment to manage the World XI in the Soccer Aid charity match a few weeks later. That was despite the awkwardness of the game being held at Stamford Bridge. They lost 6-3 to Frank Lampard’s England XI.

MIGUEL D’AGOSTINO, FIRST-TEAM COACH.

Industry observers note that to give a sense of how long Pochettino has known ‘Miki’, around 1992, Pochettino purchased his first car while a player for Newell’s Old Boys. He gave his team-mate a lift home. When D’Agostino went to get out of the car, the wind caught it hard, and broke Pochettino’s door. D'Agostino never paid the bill to have it fixed – something Pochettino occasionally likes to remind him of.

Miguel D'Agostino, known as 'Miki', has heaps of experience as a former analyst and scout.

The first-team coach has known Pochettino since 1992 (both pictured at Tottenham in 2019).

Pochettino clearly forgave his fellow defender, who was also plying his trade under Marcelo Bielsa.

Sources indicate that D’Agostino was an analyst at Espanyol, initially attached to the scouting department before assuming responsibility for filming training sessions and overseeing player analysis. From there, he followed Pochettino wherever he went, from Southampton to Tottenham to Paris Saint-Germain to Chelsea to the United States national team.

Sources indicate that while with the USA, D’Agostino would watch games in the MLS, going to Real Salt Lake or wherever there were players for scouting. In training, he is hands-on, sometimes with a stopwatch in hand or notepad containing that day’s drills.

When Pochettino tested positive for Covid-19 in January 2021, D’Agostino and Perez took temporary charge of his PSG side. They beat Angers 1-0 away from home in Ligue 1.

All of Pochettino’s confidants have a good grasp of English.

SILVIA TUYA, STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING COACH.

The newest member of Pochettino’s inner circle, having joined his USA national set-up in October 2024.

With a PhD in sports science, Tuya had worked with FC Levante Badalona in Liga F, Spain’s top tier for women’s football, while she also served as a lecturer at the National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia at the University of Barcelona.

Since teaming up with Pochettino, she was seen on the training pitch and in the gym with the players.

Tuya will become Manchester United's first-ever female coach connected with the men's team.

Silvia Tuya is the newest member of Pochettino’s team, having joined his USA set-up in 2024.

Tuya is set to become Manchester United's first-ever female coach with the men's team.

TONI JIMENEZ, GOALKEEPING COACH.

After winning gold for Spain at the Barcelona Olympics in 1992, Jimenez met Pochettino in 1994 when they became team-mates for Espanyol, but it is worth recalling the 2000 Copa del Rey final when they found themselves on opposing sides.

Industry observers note that the goalkeeper represented Atletico Madrid, and Pochettino was in defence for Espanyol, who won 2-1. After full-time, Pochettino delayed his celebrations to go and console his friend, who had already endured a challenging year with his father having passed away.

Jimenez has never forgotten that kindness from Pochettino, and like the others, the two have worked together wherever the latter has managed, from Espanyol to Southampton to Tottenham to PSG to Chelsea to the USA. They have shared a fair few of their favourite mate teas in their time, and now for United, where Jimenez will work with Senne Lammens and Co.

It has been revealed that they say training is rarely boring when Jimenez is involved. He was happy to prove to Tottenham’s players during one tour of Malaysia that he could copy Rene Higuita’s scorpion kick save, for example, and is pretty good when testing his goalkeepers in free-kick practice. Lammens should beware he is liable to do a little dance if he scores past you, however.

Recent findings suggest that hugo Lloris, the former Spurs goalkeeper who won the 2018 World Cup with France, frequently credited the charismatic Jimenez for adding new areas to his game. Pochettino has also hailed Jimenez for how he keeps second and third-choice goalkeepers motivated when they are not playing.

Hugo Lloris frequently credited Toni Jimenez (pictured) for adding fresh areas to his game.

Sebastiano Pochettino first worked with his father at Tottenham (pictured celebrating at PSG).

SEBASTIANO POCHETTINO, SPORTS SCIENTIST AND FITNESS COACH.

The son of the manager. A graduate of Southampton Solent University, Sebastiano first worked with his father at Tottenham. It was remarked that he had become the Premier League’s youngest sports scientist when he was hired at the age of 22.

He soon became a regular sight in training sessions and on match days, seen putting the players through their paces and with the substitutes as they warmed up.

Sebastiano became a fitness coach and joined his old man at PSG, Chelsea and the USA. One of his specialties is in injury prevention, and that includes monitoring the players’ sleep and mood.

Trust is important to Pochettino, and he knows he can rely on family.

Hired by the USA as their men's national team lead analyst in August 2023 - just over a year before Pochettino took charge - Scott previously spent eight years at the FA before moving to Inter Miami.

He graduated from Liverpool John Moores University, achieving a first class BsC in Science and Football, with his major project titled 'A Comparison of the Technical Demands in Academy and Reserve Team Soccer'.

He went on to complete a PhD in Exercise Psychology & Performance Analysis there, before putting his skills to use during internships at Everton and Liverpool before joining the FA.

Scott has clearly impressed Pochettino, who confirmed before Tuesday's clash with Haiti that he was among those staying with him for that game before joining United - with Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr having travelled to England already.

Sources indicate that 'I am with Miguel and Silvia and Alec [for this game],' he mentioned. 'After, they are going to join me in Manchester.'.

Mark Noble Reveals Important Change Behind West Ham’s Transfer Aims

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mark Noble has provided an interesting insight into how West Ham United’s recruitment operation is working under Scott Parker, revealing that Nils Koppen is in regular contact with the coaching staff about the players the club needs.
  • Speaking in an interview with West Ham’s official website, Noble explained that the Director of Player Recruitment is arriving at Rush Green as early as 6.30am, watching training and discussing the squad with Parker and his coaches.
  • Recent findings suggest that with the January transfer window approaching and West Ham desperate to secure promotion, it’s encouraging to hear that recruitment discussions are taking place.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mark Noble has provided an interesting insight into how West Ham United’s recruitment operation is working under Scott Parker, revealing that Nils Koppen is in regular contact with the coaching staff about the players the club needs.

Speaking in an interview with West Ham’s official website, Noble explained that the Director of Player Recruitment is arriving at Rush Green as early as 6.30am, watching training and discussing the squad with Parker and his coaches.

Recent findings suggest that with the January transfer window approaching and West Ham desperate to secure promotion, it’s encouraging to hear that recruitment discussions are taking place. But for me, the most key part of Noble’s revelation has very little to do with what time Koppen arrives for work.

Quite frankly, whether Koppen arrives at half six in the morning is neither here nor there.

Much of the analytical and recruitment work can be carried out perfectly well from wherever somebody can plug into the internet.

What I find far more important is the open dialogue Noble has described.

He explained that Koppen watches training and that the coaching staff speak openly with him about the players they believe West Ham need.

Koppen then works with the club’s scouts and analysts in the background, allowing Parker and Noble to concentrate on coaching.

That strikes me as a huge plus and potentially a massive step in the right direction.

It also appears to represent a departure from the way things have operated previously, when questions were regularly raised about whether recruitment decisions matched the manager’s requirements.

As we discussed following Parker’s talkSPORT interview, the manager is absolutely right to concentrate on improving the players already at his disposal rather than becoming consumed by January transfers.

But that only works if the recruitment department understands precisely what he needs.

We know from our recent dialogue with a club insider that Koppen has begun looking for another striker, and Noble’s comments suggest those discussions are taking place alongside the coaching staff’s assessment of the squad.

That’s exactly how it should work.

Ultimately, I’m far more interested in whether Koppen signs the right players than whether he’s the first person through the door at Rush Green.

But if the people coaching the team and those recruiting for it are finally speaking openly about what West Ham need, that has to be encouraging.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.
  • Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:12.

Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.

Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.

Despite suffering two agonising Champions League defeats in recent weeks, Roma have hardly faltered on the domestic front; they are one of only two teams still undefeated in Serie A, alongside surprise leaders Lazio.

Soon after swatting Cagliari and Udinese aside, the Giallorossi signed off for the international period with a comfortable 3-0 home victory over Sassuolo, in which rising star Rodrigo Mora scored for a third straight league game.

It was an increasingly rare clean sheet for a club boasting the most lethal attack in Italy's top flight: Roma are only the fourth team in 65 years to hit the 30-goal mark by Serie A’s 11th matchday.

Dating back to last term, Gian Piero Gasperini’s side have scored at least twice in all but one of their last 16 league fixtures, only failing to do so in Como, where Donyell Malen was sent off.

Allowed to roam freely into the opposition area, defenders have collectively contributed eight goals this season, easing any pressure on Malen, Mora and their fellow forwards.

Beginning the build-up to next month’s Derby della Capitale, Roma will now seek a fifth straight win over Parma, who they beat 3-2 on their most recent trip to Stadio Tardini, with Malen inevitably scoring twice.

In fact, Parma have lost 13 of the past 20 league meetings on home turf, so history will not be on their side this weekend.

The hosts have endured a rocky start to the season, already changing coaches, and new boss Alberto Gilardino only celebrated his first victory shortly before the break.

However, days after stunning Atalanta with a shock 3-0 win in Bergamo, his side were beaten by Bologna in the Derby dell'Emilia.

Parma were reduced to 10 men within eight minutes at the Tardini, after Abdoulaye Ndiaye was dismissed following a VAR review, and they ultimately ended up losing 2-1.

As a result, the Gialloblu sit just one point above the bottom three, with only eight points on the board so far.

The club’s second-highest Serie A scorer during his playing days, Gilardino has a more modest managerial record, and he surely faces another survival scrap after last term’s fruitless fight with Pisa.

Roma have welcomed Paulo Dybala and first-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar back during the break, but the latter’s deputy Pierluigi Gollini remains a doubt after missing two games with a back injury.

Devyne Rensch (adductor) and Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) are still sidelined, but Gasperini should have everyone else available.

A sure starter up front, Malen sits joint-second in the Capocannoniere rankings with eight Serie A goals, and the Dutch striker also scored for his country in the UEFA Nations League last week.

Meanwhile, Parma will be missing Argentine forward David Romero, who sustained a serious shoulder injury against Bologna.

Diego Carlos is also struggling with a thigh strain, injury-prone midfielder Adrian Bernabe is a big doubt, and Ndiaye must serve a one-match ban.

In the absence of Romero, teenage starlet Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is another contender.

Parma possible starting lineup:.

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Drobnic; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Lontani, Toure.

Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Soule, Mora; Malen.

Roma can pick up where they left off before the break, as a limited Parma side will struggle to match their intensity and flair.

A fourth straight win in Serie A will warm the Giallorossi up for next week's tough trip to Paris Saint-Germain.

Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that this was the definition of a hard-earned point.
  • Industry observers note that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
  • Industry observers note that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that this was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Industry observers note that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Industry observers note that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

It has been revealed that “It reveals where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

Sources indicate that “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads revealed massive character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

Industry observers note that in truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a fresh manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

Sources indicate that it is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

In a recent development, bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another upcoming signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Industry observers note that bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

According to recent reports, that is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

According to recent reports, speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads demonstrated the right reaction.”.

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx.

According to recent reports, it’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9.

Despite having a miserable record against Bournemouth in recent years, Newcastle will be expected to win this afternoon. The atmosphere, electric for the opener against Liverpool and the return of villain Alexander Isak, will be more expectant today.

These are the fixtures Eddie Howe’s team repeatedly slipped up in at home last season, where the likes of Everton, Brentford, Bournemouth and Sunderland all won.

Can Jaissle improve that record? Can his team thrive when they are likely to have more of the ball, play against a low block defence and an opponent adept at lightning-fast counterattacks?

Does the German’s “vertical” football have as much success against a team that does not play a high defensive line as Liverpool and Tottenham did?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the new season but have people got a little carried away?

Let’s see how they get on against a Bournemouth side that probably should have got at least a point away to Manchester City in their opening away game.

They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

In a recent development, despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. Newly introduced signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Industry observers note that west Ham return to action tomorrow with a home tie against visitors Preston North End – a team who sit rock bottom of the Championship but are not without their recent triumphs after turning over promotion-chasing Southampton just before the break. So West Ham need to be wary, despite their opponents’ lowly league table position.

With Scott Parker having enjoyed an unbroken two week training period during the break, West Ham fans will now surely get to see the ‘Parker XI’ rather than Nuno’s inherited lin-up with which he began the first two games of his West Ham tenure.

The first visible difference will surely be to see -shock, horror – players used in their correct positions: Nuno because infamous for using square pegs in round holes – Morato at left back being the case in point.

Morata’s days at left back are surely over.

Despite being signed as a centre back and having played all but 33 of his last 177 games as such, Nuno insisted on using the 6’3 Brazilian – hardily the most mobile – as a left back who was frequently found to be out of position, often allowing wingers to get the better of him: Scott Parker hooked him at half time after a pretty inept left-back performance against Cardiff.

Sources indicate that with centre back Maximilian Kilman suspended for tomorrow’s clash there should be no more Morato at left back – incredibly West Ham fans have never seen the loanee in his preferred specialist position until now. Ezra Mayers has already done enough to start at left back leaving Parker free to slot Morato into the role for which he was signed, alongside Mavropanos.

In a recent development, square pegs into square holes: Scott Parker’s secret weapon in his West Ham reboot. Who’d have thought.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:19, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:21.

Separated by one place and one point, Napoli and Torino will return to Serie A duty on Saturday evening, when they meet at Stadio Maradona.

Both sides entered the international break on a grim run of form, sparking talk of another crisis for the hosts.

After setting out with lofty ambitions, Napoli sit 10th in Serie A after 11 matchdays and have lost three of their first four Champions League fixtures.

Struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, the Partenopei have won just five times across all competitions since Massimiliano Allegri succeeded Antonio Conte.

That represents their lowest tally of wins at this stage of a campaign since 2003, when they drew 10 of their first 15 games down in Serie B.

Before international football intervened, Allegri's men did earn some credit by holding league leaders Lazio to a 1-1 home draw, having previously suffered damaging defeats to Juventus and Porto.

While they ended their visitors' streak of six consecutive wins - and spurned several second-half chances to seize victory - Napoli ultimately slipped further behind in the top four race.

As a result, the Campanian club cannot afford to drop many more points at the Maradona, where they beat Torino 2-1 in March - their 15th win from the last 22 league meetings.

Torino's only two triumphs during that period both came in Turin, so their last top-flight win in Naples dates all the way back to 2009.

Like their hosts, it has been a mixed start to the season under latest management: Ignazio Abate's reign began slowly, but Toro then posted their best run of league wins for six years, before suddenly faltering again.

Having previously taken maximum points from three consecutive games, Toro lost to high-flyers Como and Frosinone, then went into the break with a disappointing home draw against Lecce.

Nonetheless, the Granata have claimed 14 points from their first 11 games for the fifth time in six years, leaving them just one behind Napoli in standings.

So, with a win this weekend, Abate can surpass his former Milan coach Allegri, as ambitious apprentice meets fading master.

Napoli form (all competitions):.

Napoli are still burdened by a significant absence list, but Allegri will have three players back at his disposal on Saturday: David Neres and Costantino Favasuli have recovered from muscular injuries, while Luca Marianucci has served his suspension.

Alisson Santos, Benoit Badiashile, Stanislav Lobotka, captain Giovanni Di Lorenzo and former Torino skipper Alessandro Buongiorno are still unavailable.

Having starred in Belgium's massive UEFA Nations League victory over Italy, top scorer Kevin De Bruyne will aim to build on his six goal involvements for the Partenopei this season.

While speculation has been stirred up about De Bruyne's future, fan favourite Scott McTominay is set to stay put for now, and he has found the net three times in two games against Torino.

McTominay's international teammate Che Adams is Toro's leading Serie A scorer on four; the Scotland striker could partner Giovanni Simeone, who only scored six times in 83 league appearances for Napoli but has previously scored five goals against them.

Typically lining up just behind the front pair, Nikola Vlasic missed Sunday's clash between Croatia and the Czech Republic due to a minor thigh strain, but he is still expected to play this weekend.

However, Abate has fitness doubts regarding wing-backs Rafik Belghali, Ricardo Rodriguez and Niccolo Fortini.

Napoli possible starting lineup:.

Meret; Beukema, Rrahmani, Marin; Politano, Anguissa, De Bruyne, McTominay, Spinazzola; Vergara; Hojlund.

Torino possible starting lineup:.

Perri; Coco, Ismajli, Comuzzo; Belghali, Fitz-Jim, Mandragora, Cacciamani; Vlasic; Adams, Simeone.

After two defeats and one draw from their last three games, both teams will be desperate for a win.

While Napoli are hampered by injuries and appear disunited, Torino have been leaking too many goals, so more frustration could be on the cards.

Published: 05:25 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 08:02 EST, 17 November 2026.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.

The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.

Industry observers note that the Championship side announced his departure with a statement from Mowbray. It read: 'Unfortunately, due to health concerns, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

Industry observers note that 'I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

In a recent development, 'Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

Recent findings suggest that 'To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers boss due to ill health.

'I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Pasha, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

'I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. Thank you for your understanding.'.

Industry observers note that mowbray leaves with Blackburn 13th in the Championship. He took over at the club in June this year having spent two years out of the game following his health concerns at Birmingham City.

The veteran manager suddenly stepped down as manager of Birmingham in February 2024 after undergoing surgery for bowel cancer. He had 15cm of his bowel removed during his treatment.

He took a temporary leave of absence after eight games in charge, before officially resigning from the role in May.

Mowbray, who has managed a host of English clubs, opened up publicly about his struggles, telling the Times that his children had feared the worst.

It has been revealed that 'I had the conversation with my family and you could see they were frightened,' he mentioned. 'Was I frightened? My only thoughts were for my family, my three children and my wife and making sure they were OK.

Recent findings suggest that 'I had to put everything in order and I tried to. My wife saw our banking app for the first time in her life. It's little things like that. She understood. This was serious stuff. I felt she needed to know where we had our money, whether it was ISAs or pensions and what was in the bank.'.

Sources indicate that speaking on his diagnosis, which came after he collapsed when trying to answer the door, he added: 'My wife put me in the car and drove me back to hospital and they wanted to know why I was collapsing and in the condition I was,' he states. 'They rehydrated me and put me on a drip overnight.

It has been revealed that 'I remember sitting there in bed and my kids' eyes were watering up. They were scared I wasn't going to live. How old were they? They were 15, 17 and 19. I could see the fear in their eyes.'.

Mowbray's comeback story when he was made Blackburn boss in the summer was one of the feel-good moments of the offseason. It has not been disclosed what his current health issue is.

Mowbray leaves Blackburn with the team in 13th place in the Championship table.

Blackburn Rovers owner Balaji Rao added his own statement, writing: 'Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

'Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

Sources indicate that 'Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.'.

Chief Executive Officer Steve Curwood said: 'Tony’s passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he reveals for players, staff and those around him that mean so much.

'Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.

'On behalf of everyone at Blackburn Rovers, I would like to send Tony and his family our very best wishes during this time.'.

Bayer Leverkusen will hope to keep pace with the Bundesliga's top four on Saturday, when they take on visitors SC Paderborn at BayArena.

The hosts come into the clash with 16 points after nine matchweeks and could end the weekend five points from the top four, whereas 13th-placed Paderborn have 10 points.

Leverkusen are two points from fourth-placed RB Leipzig and three points from third-placed Freiburg, but only four points separate them from 11th-placed Hamburger SV.

Manager Carles Martinez oversaw a 2-1 victory against FC Koln on November 8 prior to the international break, and that brought to an end a losing streak of two games.

The hosts have also lost two of their last three Bundesliga fixtures, conceding eight goals while scoring on four occasions.

Leverkusen's two most recent home clashes saw them lose 1-0 against Marseille in the Europa League on November 5 and 4-2 against Stuttgart in the German top flight on October 31.

However, it should be noted that they triumphed in each of their first five clashes at BayArena this season, netting at least two goals in each contest.

Paderborn were held to a 2-2 stalemate by Eintracht Frankfurt on November 7 before the international break, and that extended their undefeated streak in the league to four outings.

The club only won once in that time, while they managed to score five goals and keep two clean sheets, with all four of the goals they conceded coming in two separate 2-2 draws.

Head coach Ralf Kettemann will hope to earn a first away victory in five matches, though a draw would be the club's fourth in that period.

The visitors have failed to find the back of the net in three of their four Bundesliga matches on the road this campaign, though they also prevented opponents from scoring twice.

A win for Paderborn would be their first ever success against Leverkusen, with the hosts having beaten the visitors in six of their seven meetings.

Midfielders Aleix Garcia and Ezequiel Fernandez are likely candidates for the team's double pivot, and they may play ahead of centre-backs Edmond Tapsoba and Facundo Medina.

Paderborn's only confirmed absentee is attacker Timur Gayret, who is not scheduled to return until January due to a knee injury.

It would not be surprising to see the visitors field a front two of Marvin Pieringer and Stefano Marino ahead of midfielders Tom Baack, Santiago Castaneda and Gabriel Vidovic.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and can profoundly influence individual fitness and population dynamics1,2. Although the ecological and social conditions that favour cannibalism have been well documented2, the molecular signals that trigger cannibalistic attacks have remained poorly understood. Here we show that in Locusta migratoria, guaiacol, a volatile compound with augmented release after injury, attracts gregarious nymphs and induces cannibalistic behaviour. Guaiacol is detected by olfactory receptors LmOR36 and LmOR34, and disruption of either receptor abolishes attraction, thereby impairing induction of cannibalism. Guaiacol is synthesized by haemolymph symbiont Enterobacter hormaechei. Injury promotes bacterial congregation at the wound site, leading to elevated guaiacol production through a clustered set of vanillic acid decarboxylase genes; deletion of this gene cluster abolishes guaiacol production and its behavioural effects. Notably, guaiacol initially functions as a beneficial signal after injury. Guaiacol activates immune-related pathways in wounded locusts, enhancing pathogen resistance and increasing survival following minor injury. However, when guaiacol emission exceeds a threshold determined by injury severity, it functions as an external cue that attracts cannibals. Cannibalistic locusts exploit this immune-related odour to locate severely injured conspecifics, gaining both nutritional resources and immune system benefits. Together, our findings identify a microbial–chemical mechanism that links immune defence with cannibalistic behaviour and provide potential molecular targets for manipulation of cannibalism-dependent population dynamics.

Recent findings suggest that cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and is often considered to be an adaptive behaviour driven by ecological or social pressures1,2. However, its occurrence is highly context-dependent, and the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. In humans, cannibalism largely disappeared with cultural evolution, partly owing to prion diseases3. Similarly, insects such as crickets rarely engage in cannibalism under normal conditions, but confinement or nutritional deprivation can trigger this behaviour4. These observations highlight the influence of environmental pressures on cannibalism, although its intrinsic regulatory mechanisms remain unclear.

Recent findings suggest that locusts provide a compelling model for studies of cannibalism because of its notable role in collective dynamics5,6. In juvenile migratory bands, the threat of conspecific predation from behind promotes forward movement, reducing cannibalistic risk and contributing to group cohesion5,6. Cannibalism also provides nutritional benefits, allowing locusts to compensate for food deficiencies and potentially enhancing survival and movement capacity7,8. This behaviour is strongly influenced by density-dependent phase polyphenism. At low densities, solitarious locusts avoid conspecifics, whereas increased population density promotes gregarious behaviour and cannibalistic encounters5,7. Nutritional deficiencies further exacerbate cannibalism. Field studies of South American locusts (Schistocerca cancellata) have demonstrated that carbohydrate deprivation promotes cannibalism9, whereas laboratory studies on desert locusts (Schistocerca gregaria) have shown that protein-biased diets reduce movement and increase cannibalistic interactions7. Although these findings establish the ecological importance of cannibalism, its molecular and genetic regulation remains poorly understood.

It has been revealed that chemical cues regulate diverse locust behaviours, including aggregation10,11, oviposition12, mating13 and cannibalism14. Our previous work identified phenylacetonitrile (PAN) as a density-dependent anticannibalistic pheromone that activates specific olfactory receptors and reduces conspecific predation in crowded populations14. However, whether chemical cues actively induce cannibalism has remained unclear. Field and laboratory observations indicate that injured locusts are preferentially targeted by conspecifics15, suggesting that injury-induced chemical signals may attract individuals and promote cannibalistic behaviour.

Guaiacol, a volatile compound produced by gut microbiota during plant digestion, has been identified as an aggregation pheromone in desert locusts16. Here we show that injury-induced microbiota-derived guaiacol coordinates immune defence and cannibalism in migratory locusts (Locusta migratoria) and elucidate the underlying mechanisms, which span microbial biosynthesis, olfactory detection, immune regulation and behavioural responses. Together, our findings identify a microbial signalling mechanism linking immunity and cannibalism, revealing how host–microbe interactions mediate a trade-off between immune protection and vulnerability to conspecific predation.

It has been revealed that cannibalism in L. migratoria exhibits phase polyphenism, with solitarious nymphs typically avoiding conspecific predation, whereas gregarious nymphs are more prone to engage in cannibalism, particularly under conditions of crowding or food scarcity14. Preliminary observations indicated that injured individuals were rapidly surrounded and attacked by nearby conspecifics (Fig. 1a), suggesting that injury itself serves as a cue that increases susceptibility to conspecific predation. To test this hypothesis, we conducted dual-choice assays with gregarious fourth- and fifth-instar nymphs, the developmental stages at which cannibalism is most prevalent14. As injury can alter locomotor performance and therefore influence predator choice independently of injury-derived signals, we controlled for this potentially confounding factor by immobilizing both prey individuals. This experimental design enabled us to specifically evaluate the contribution of injury-associated cues to predator preference. In each assay, pairs of immobilized intact and injured fourth-instar nymphs were presented at opposite ends of a chamber containing ten starved fifth-instar predators (Fig. 1b). Injuries were induced either mechanically or by previous conspecific bites. Across all assays, predators consistently exhibited a marked predation preference for injured over intact prey, indicating a significant role of injury in heightening vulnerability to conspecific predation (Fig. 1c).

To determine whether the type of injury influenced predation preference, we compared predator preferences between mechanically injured and bitten prey. No significant difference was observed (Fig. 1c), indicating that injury alone, regardless of its origin, is sufficient to induce preferential predation. To explore whether injury-induced vulnerability was consistent across developmental stages, we extended the assays to first- to fifth-instar nymphs as prey. In all stages tested, fifth-instar predators consistently preferred injured prey over their intact counterparts, irrespective of injury type (Extended Data Fig. 1a). These findings demonstrate that injury-driven cannibalism is a robust and consistent trait across the development of gregarious locusts.

Industry observers note that next, we investigated the sensory cues mediating injury-induced predation. To assess the roles of olfactory and visual inputs, we performed antennal ablation (disrupting primary olfactory input), knocked out olfactory coreceptor LmOrco (disrupting olfactory receptor function) (Extended Data Fig. 1b) or removed the compound eyes (disrupting visual input). Predators with removed compound eyes retained their preference for injured prey (Fig. 1d), suggesting that visual cues are not required to mediate this behaviour. By contrast, predators lacking antennae or LmOrco function demonstrated no preference for injured over intact prey (Fig. 1e,f). Notably, although antennectomized predators no longer exhibited a statistically significant preference, a weak residual bias towards injured prey remained (Fig. 1e). This observation was consistent with the anatomical organization of the locust olfactory system, in which the antennae constitute the principal but not the exclusive olfactory organs. Consequently, antennal removal might substantially reduce but not completely eliminate olfactory perception. By contrast, disruption of LmOrco, which broadly impairs odorant receptor function, resulted in a complete loss of discriminatory behaviour (Fig. 1f). Together, these findings identify LmOrco-dependent olfaction as the primary sensory modality mediating injury-induced cannibalistic predation.

According to recent reports, finally, we assessed whether volatile chemical cues contributed to the observed predation bias. Headspace volatiles from both injured and intact nymphs were collected and presented in a dual-choice olfactometer (Fig. 1g). Starved fifth-instar predators strongly preferred the zone containing volatiles from injured individuals over the zone containing volatiles from intact prey (Fig. 1h). No significant difference in preference was observed between volatiles from mechanically versus bitten prey (Fig. 1h), indicating that injury-induced volatile release enhances predator attraction, thereby increasing the susceptibility of injured individuals to cannibalism. By contrast, LmOrco−/− predators showed no preference for the zone containing volatiles from injured individuals (Fig. 1i), indicating that LmOrco-dependent olfaction mediated the predation preference.

In a recent development, to investigate the chemical signals underlying injury-induced cannibalism in L. migratoria, we analysed the headspace volatiles emitted by intact, mechanically injured and bitten locust nymphs (Fig. 2a). Among the compounds detected, guaiacol emerged as the dominant injury-affected odorant (Fig. 2b and Extended Data Table 1), with emission levels approximately ten-fold higher in injured nymphs compared with intact controls and gregarious adults (Fig. 2b,c and Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). This increase in guaiacol release was consistent across all developmental instars (first to fifth) (Extended Data Fig. 2c), suggesting that an increase in guaiacol production is a consistent physiological response to injury in gregarious nymphs. By contrast, other compounds—including PAN, which has previously been linked to suppression of cannibalism14—highlighted no significant changes across injury conditions (Fig. 2b,c and Extended Data Fig. 2d), indicating that guaiacol is a key injury cue.

Sources indicate that to assess the behavioural significance of guaiacol, we conducted dual-choice olfactometer assays with fifth-instar nymphs and male and female adults from both gregarious and solitarious phases, testing the effects of synthetic guaiacol (Extended Data Table 2) at a concentration of 10−3 (Fig. 2d). Only gregarious nymphs exhibited strong attraction to guaiacol; solitarious individuals and gregarious adults revealed no significant preference (Fig. 2e and Supplementary Video 1). This indicated that guaiacol selectively attracts gregarious nymphs. We then investigated whether the naturally emitted levels of guaiacol from injured gregarious nymphs were sufficient to trigger attraction. Quantitative headspace analysis showed that emissions from injured gregarious nymphs corresponded to concentrations equivalent to 10−5 to 10−4 dilutions of synthetic guaiacol (Extended Data Fig. 2e). To determine whether these natural guaiacol emissions were sufficient to induce attraction, we tested behavioural responses of gregarious nymphs using a full concentration series (10−7 to 10−2) in a two-choice olfactometer (Fig. 2d). Attraction to guaiacol emerged sharply at 10−6 and remained robust at higher concentrations but disappeared at 10−7 (Fig. 2f). This aligned with the physiological range of natural emissions from injured nymphs, confirming that guaiacol concentrations released by injured individuals are behaviourally relevant. As all preceding behavioural assays were conducted with individually tested locusts, we next examined whether guaiacol attraction was preserved under the social conditions that characterize gregarious populations. To address this question, we performed dual-choice olfactometer assays using groups of five gregarious nymphs and quantified the average time spent by the group on each side of the arena. Consistent with the results obtained from individually tested animals, groups of gregarious nymphs spent significantly more time on the side containing 10−3 guaiacol than on the control side (Extended Data Fig. 2f and Supplementary Video 2). These findings demonstrate that the attractive effect of guaiacol persists in a group context and therefore probably operates under ecologically relevant social conditions.

As attraction alone does not necessarily imply a decision to engage in cannibalistic behaviour, we next investigated whether guaiacol could directly trigger cannibalistic predation. We performed two-choice predation assays, providing pairs of intact fourth-instar gregarious nymphs—one treated with 2 µl of 10−4 guaiacol (representing natural emission levels from injured nymphs) (Extended Data Fig. 2e) and the other with solvent oil—to 10 starved fifth-instar gregarious predators (Fig. 2g). Guaiacol-treated nymphs were preferentially consumed, whereas solvent-treated nymphs were rarely attacked (Fig. 2h), confirming that guaiacol is a potent elicitor of cannibalistic predation. We then sought to rule out the potential influence of endogenous guaiacol on predator preference. Previous studies have shown that guaiacol is primarily synthesized by gut microbiota during plant digestion in locusts16. To eliminate this confounding factor, we generated germ-depleted gregarious nymphs by administering a cocktail of three antibiotics (tetracycline, streptomycin and ciprofloxacin) in their feed17,18,19 (Fig. 2i). This approach effectively abolished guaiacol emission in both intact and injured nymphs, providing a chemically clean background for subsequent behavioural assays (Fig. 2j). We then treated the germ-depleted gregarious nymphs with 2 µl of either 10−4 guaiacol (mimicking natural release from injured nymphs) (Extended Data Fig. 2e) or solvent oil and used them as prey in dual-choice predation assays (Fig. 2i). As observed previously, guaiacol-treated nymphs were preferentially attacked, and solvent-treated nymphs were largely ignored (Fig. 2k and Extended Data Fig. 2g). Finally, to evaluate the ecological relevance of guaiacol-mediated cannibalism under more naturalistic conditions, we performed semi-field experiments in large outdoor mesh enclosures (1.8 m × 1.2 m × 1.5 m). Each enclosure contained 500 fifth-instar gregarious predators, together with 100 fourth-instar prey perfumed with either 10−4 guaiacol or solvent alone (Extended Data Fig. 2h). After 24 h, substantially fewer fourth-instar nymphs remained in guaiacol-treated enclosures than in control enclosures, indicating a significantly higher frequency of cannibalistic interactions in the presence of guaiacol (Extended Data Fig. 2h). Consistent with direct behavioural observations, the reduction in surviving individuals was attributable to increased conspecific predation rather than escape, as all locusts were confined within the enclosure. These findings demonstrate that guaiacol-mediated promotion of cannibalism persists at the population level under seminatural conditions, supporting the ecological relevance of this injury-associated signal. Collectively, these findings establish guaiacol as a critical chemical cue that both signals injury and induces conspecific predation.

Recent findings suggest that to elucidate the molecular basis of guaiacol detection in L. migratoria, we sought to identify the specific olfactory receptors involved. In our previous study, we identified LmOR34, LmOR36 and LmOR39 as receptors responsive to guaiacol, on the basis of functional characterization of 49 L. migratoria olfactory receptors20. To confirm whether other olfactory receptors were involved in detection of this compound, we expanded our analysis to include a panel of 82 of approximately 140 identified L. migratoria olfactory receptors (Fig. 3a). Consistent with our earlier findings, LmOR34, LmOR36 and LmOR39 exhibited robust responses to guaiacol in a heterologous expression system (Fig. 3a,b), while no other receptor showed comparable sensitivity.
